title: ginwind/VLA-JEPA
summary: VLA-JEPA targets vision-language-action robot policies by adding a latent world model that predicts future representations rather than raw observations. The project is an ECCV 2026 codebase for experimenting with this JEPA-style predictive objective as a way to improve action learning from visual and language-conditioned context.

It narrows the usual CV/NLP interview scope to robotics-specific problems, making it useful as a field primer and preparation resource rather than a general machine learning handbook.

title: leggedrobotics/pace-sim2real
summary: PACE targets sim-to-real transfer for legged robots by identifying actuator and joint dynamics using only standard joint encoders, rather than relying on extra sensing or detailed proprietary actuator models. The repo appears useful for making legged-robot simulations better match hardware behavior, especially where unmodeled drivetrain and joint effects are a major source of transfer failure.

summary: google-deepmind/mujoco_playground is an open-source library for training robot policies with GPU-accelerated MuJoCo simulations and carrying them toward real-world deployment. It is aimed at sim-to-real workflows, giving researchers a practical playground for running fast robot learning experiments rather than building the simulation and training infrastructure from scratch.

title: NVIDIA/warp
summary: NVIDIA Warp is a Python toolkit for writing GPU-accelerated simulation code, with an emphasis on robotics, physics-style environments, and machine learning workflows. It is useful when researchers need custom high-performance kernels and differentiable simulation components without dropping fully into low-level CUDA.

extra.full_text: A Python framework for GPU-accelerated simulation, robotics, and machine learning.

title: RobotControlStack/robot-control-stack
summary: RobotControlStack provides a compact sim-to-real stack for training and deploying VLA models and reinforcement-learning agents without relying on ROS. It wraps MuJoCo environments in Gymnasium with synchronous execution, targeting common robot platforms including Franka, UR5e, xArm, SO101, and YAM, which makes it useful for researchers who want a lighter path from simulation experiments to hardware deployment.

extra.full_text: A lean, ROS-free sim-to-real framework for training and deploying Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models and RL agents. Native MuJoCo Gymnasium wrappers with synchronous execution for Franka, UR5e, xArm, SO101 and YAM.

title: isaac-sim/IsaacLab-Arena
summary: Isaac Lab - Arena extends NVIDIA Isaac Lab with a composable simulation stack for building robot learning environments from interchangeable robots, objects, tasks, and scenes. It is aimed at rapid prototyping and policy evaluation across diverse embodiments and environment configurations, making it useful for stress-testing how learned robotic behaviors transfer across simulated setups.

extra.full_text: Isaac Lab - Arena is a robotics simulation framework that enhances NVIDIA Isaac Lab by providing a composable, scalable system for creating diverse simulation environments and evaluating robot learning policies. The framework enables developers to rapidly prototype and test robotic tasks with various robot embodiments, objects, and environments.

title: ROBOTIS-GIT/cyclo_lab
summary: ROBOTIS-GIT/cyclo_lab packages tutorials for training ROBOTIS robots with reinforcement learning and imitation learning, with a path from simulated training to deployment on physical hardware. Its useful focus is Sim2Real: researchers can prototype learned policies in simulation and then move them onto real ROBOTIS platforms rather than treating the repo as simulation-only teaching material.

extra.full_text: This repository provides tutorials for reinforcement learning and imitation learning using ROBOTIS robots, and supports Sim2Real functionality for deploying the learned policies on real robots.

title: iit-DLSLab/basic-locomotion-isaaclab
summary: An IsaacLab DirectEnv implementation for basic quadruped locomotion, aimed at training and testing policies across multiple robot platforms. It is useful as a starting point for sim-to-sim and sim-to-real locomotion pipelines, rather than a standalone benchmark or paper result.

extra.full_text: An IsaacLab DirectEnv for basic quadrupedal locomotion tasks, with support for multiple quadruped robots, sim-to-sim, and sim-to-real pipelines

title: RoboVerseOrg/RoboVerse
summary: RoboVerse aims to unify the robot-learning pipeline around a shared platform, dataset, and benchmark for training and evaluating scalable, generalizable robot policies. It is positioned as infrastructure for researchers who need a common environment to compare methods across robot tasks and datasets rather than stitching together separate simulators, data formats, and evaluation setups.

extra.full_text: RoboVerse: Towards a Unified Platform, Dataset and Benchmark for Scalable and Generalizable Robot Learning

summary: AirStack is an agent-native robotics stack aimed at moving embodied AI from simulation to field hardware quickly, using a closed-loop one-to-one workflow that mirrors the real robot and validates itself against hardware behavior. summary: An IsaacLab DirectEnv setup for training and evaluating quadruped locomotion policies when one or more motors fail.
